title: Opening an image may drop the reader out of full screen
acceptance: On a real iPad: open an article, tap an image, dismiss it, and observe whether the reader is still full screen with the library column still collapsed
If it is, close this — there is no bug
If the library column reappears or the reader leaves full screen, it is real and becomes an implementation task
notes: Converted to a human check on 2026-08-25 after an agent spent 152k tokens and could not deliver a single tap: this sandbox has no display session at all — screencapture fails with "could not create image from display" — so no GUI automation is possible. It behaved correctly throughout: reverted its instrumentation, left the tree clean, landed nothing, declined to force past Homebrew tap-trust for a side tool, and disclosed the two tools it had installed (since removed). THE QUESTION IS TEN SECONDS OF HUMAN TIME ON HARDWARE THE OWNER ALREADY HAS. ReaderView.onDisappear calls onImmersiveChange(false), and RootView uses that to restore the split view. If SwiftUI fires onDisappear when a descendant presents a fullScreenCover — which ArticleBlockView now does for images — tapping a picture would bring the library column back behind the cover. Open an article on the iPad, tap an image, dismiss, look.
